title: Vireo after PR 172
eyebrow: Vireo engine · Windows (RTX 5060 Laptop, 8 GB) · 2026-11-15, night · main at 99c47ed (PRs 171 and 172 merged) · four small models at Q4 · reading, writing and first token at four prompt sizes
headline: Within 8% of llama.cpp reading long prompts, ahead at 113K on Qwen 3.5 4B, and the Gemmas' writing after 125K tokens back up
lede: The run after PR 169 repeated on the merged build, the same contexts and prompts, one run each through both servers with streaming. PR 172's 128-token tiles lift the Qwens' reading: Vireo is {since:vireo|long.read_tps} faster on the ~32K prompt than after PR 169 and {since:vireo|medium.read_tps} on ~3K, while llama.cpp, unchanged, moved {since:llama|long.read_tps} and {since:llama|medium.read_tps}. Against llama.cpp Vireo now reads the ~32K prompt {long.read_tps} (after PR 169: {old:long.read_tps}) and the largest prompts {xlarge.read_tps}, ahead on Qwen 3.5 4B at 113K tokens. PR 171 stops the guesses deep in a chat: writing after the largest prompt is {xlarge.gen_tps} against llama.cpp (after PR 169: {old:xlarge.gen_tps}), with Gemma 4 E2B and E4B each {since:Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|xlarge.gen_tps} since then.

cards.text: Vireo reading the ~32K prompt against llama.cpp (after PR 169: {old:long.read_tps}); Vireo itself {since:vireo|long.read_tps} since, the Qwens the most
reading the largest prompt each model fits on 8 GB; Qwen 3.5 4B ahead ({Qwen 3.5 4B|xlarge.read_tps}) at 113,192 tokens, Gemma 4 E2B furthest behind
writing after the largest prompt (after PR 169: {old:xlarge.gen_tps}); the Gemmas' draft models no longer slow E4B there
writing after ~3K tokens: the Gemmas' draft models +40% and +54%, the Qwens level

rig.label: Software
rig.detail: main with PRs 171 and 172 merged, cargo build --release · llama.cpp b12262 (CUDA build, -fa on, -ngl 99, -np 1) · vireo-server with --context and --thinking off

where: Small (a ~40-token question). Vireo first to the first token on all four ({short.ttft}; times of 30-120 ms, so the percentages swing). Writing ahead on the Gemmas ({Gemma 4 E2B|short.gen_tps}, {Gemma 4 E4B|short.gen_tps}, their draft models), level on the Qwens ({Qwen 3.5 4B|short.gen_tps}, {Qwen 3.5 9B|short.gen_tps}). Reading so few tokens is mostly fixed overhead and says little.

Medium (~3K tokens). Reading level on Gemma 4 E4B ({Gemma 4 E4B|medium.read_tps}), a little behind on E2B ({Gemma 4 E2B|medium.read_tps}, the first server's one-off below; drafting off it reads {plain:Gemma 4 E2B|medium.read_tps} against llama.cpp), behind on the Qwens ({Qwen 3.5 4B|medium.read_tps}, {Qwen 3.5 9B|medium.read_tps}, from −11% and −20%). Writing well ahead on the Gemmas ({Gemma 4 E2B|medium.gen_tps}, {Gemma 4 E4B|medium.gen_tps}), level on the Qwens. First token {medium.ttft}.

Large (~32K tokens). Reading behind on all four but by less: {Gemma 4 E4B|long.read_tps} on Gemma 4 E4B, {Gemma 4 E2B|long.read_tps} on E2B, {Qwen 3.5 4B|long.read_tps} and {Qwen 3.5 9B|long.read_tps} on the Qwens (after PR 169 −12% and −14%); first token the same. Writing ahead on the Gemmas ({Gemma 4 E2B|long.gen_tps}, {Gemma 4 E4B|long.gen_tps}), behind on the Qwens ({Qwen 3.5 4B|long.gen_tps}, {Qwen 3.5 9B|long.gen_tps}).

Xlarge (the largest that fits). Reading ahead on Qwen 3.5 4B ({Qwen 3.5 4B|xlarge.read_tps}, first token too), level on Gemma 4 E4B ({Gemma 4 E4B|xlarge.read_tps}), behind on Qwen 3.5 9B ({Qwen 3.5 9B|xlarge.read_tps}) and Gemma 4 E2B ({Gemma 4 E2B|xlarge.read_tps}). Writing level on Gemma 4 E4B ({Gemma 4 E4B|xlarge.gen_tps}) and Qwen 3.5 9B ({Qwen 3.5 9B|xlarge.gen_tps}), behind on Qwen 3.5 4B ({Qwen 3.5 4B|xlarge.gen_tps}) and Gemma 4 E2B ({Gemma 4 E2B|xlarge.gen_tps}; drafting off {plain:Gemma 4 E2B|xlarge.gen_tps}).
method: Small, medium and large: evals/speed/bench-2026-11-13/bench.py with ENGINES=vireo,vireo-plain,llama MODELS=e2b,e4b,q4b,q9b REPS=1 WORK=short,medium,long and python -X utf8 -I, at 65,536 (32,768 for Qwen 3.5 9B). Xlarge: bench-2026-11-15-windows-after-pr172/xlarge.py (the after-PR-169 run's script) at the contexts found then, 131,072 for the Gemmas with all of xlarge.txt, 114,688 for Qwen 3.5 4B with it cut to 396,000 characters, 49,152 for Qwen 3.5 9B cut to 166,000, the same text for both engines; shared GPU memory read after loading and after the prompt. Each server warmed up with a five-word chat first; one server on the GPU at a time. Speeds are the servers' own (Vireo's log, llama.cpp's timings); first token is client-side. Every cell's change is against bench-2026-11-15-windows-after-pr169, the same workloads. Results: results.jsonl (48 rows), xlarge.jsonl (12), recheck-e2b-medium.jsonl; page: evals/speed/bench_after_pr172_report.py.

notes.read_tps: Prompt tokens read ÷ the time reading them, as each server reports it. Vireo keeps its ~1,300 (Gemma) or ~1,480 (Qwen) tokens of instructions from the warm-up chat and does not read them again. Since after PR 169: Vireo {since:vireo|medium.read_tps} on ~3K, {since:vireo|long.read_tps} on ~32K and {since:vireo|xlarge.read_tps} on the largest; llama.cpp, unchanged, {since:llama|medium.read_tps}, {since:llama|long.read_tps} and {since:llama|xlarge.read_tps}.
notes.gen_tps: Vireo as shipped: the Gemmas with Google's draft models, both families with the chat's guesses, which since PR 171 stop for a reply when too few are taken deep in a chat (past 24,000 tokens, a draft model's past 48,000). Answers differ in length between engines (the settings table has the counts); the large and xlarge answers are short (36-66 tokens), so those speeds are rougher.
notes.ttft: Seconds from sending the request to the first streamed token, on the client. Shown as llama.cpp ÷ Vireo − 1, so positive is Vireo quicker. The small prompt's first tokens take 30-120 ms on both engines, so their percentages and changes are noise-sized.
notes.plain: vireo-server with --mtp off --lookup 0: no draft model and no guesses, the same contexts and prompts. Bold is Vireo's writing speed with drafting off, then its difference from llama.cpp; under it, Vireo as shipped and how much drafting adds, and both settings' change since after PR 169. After ~125K tokens drafting now costs Gemma 4 E2B {Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|xlarge.gen_tps} against {Gemma 4 E2B|vireo-plain|xlarge.gen_tps} tokens/s (after PR 169: {old:Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|xlarge.gen_tps} against {old:Gemma 4 E2B|vireo-plain|xlarge.gen_tps}) and Gemma 4 E4B nothing ({Gemma 4 E4B|vireo|xlarge.gen_tps} against {Gemma 4 E4B|vireo-plain|xlarge.gen_tps}).
notes.settings: Context is the --context / -c each server ran with, the same for both engines in a row and the same as after PR 169. Prompt tokens are as each server counted them, with how many it kept from earlier (Vireo keeps its instructions; llama.cpp its ~24-token chat start). Shared GPU memory not growing between load and after the prompt is the check that nothing spilled into the PC's memory: it held on all twelve xlarge rows.
notes.probes: Not searched again: the contexts found after PR 169 (Qwen 3.5 4B spilled at 131,072, Qwen 3.5 9B at 57,344; xlarge-probes.jsonl there) were used as they were, and shared GPU memory stayed at its value at load on every server, 0.07 GB on Vireo and 0.16-0.24 GB on llama.cpp.

odd: Gemma 4 E2B as shipped read the ~3K prompt at {Gemma 4 E2B|vireo|medium.read_tps} tokens/s in the main run, against {Gemma 4 E2B|vireo-plain|medium.read_tps} with drafting off. It is the third run in a row where this happens to the first server of the run (12,767 after PR 169, 13,927 that afternoon). Re-run alone afterwards, both settings, short, medium, short, medium (recheck-e2b-medium.jsonl): 18,018 every time. Something about the first server after the vireo-cli speed check, not the draft model; the page keeps the main run's numbers.

Gemma 4 E4B's small prompt read at {Gemma 4 E4B|vireo|short.read_tps} tokens/s as shipped against {old:Gemma 4 E4B|vireo|short.read_tps} after PR 169 ({since:Gemma 4 E4B|vireo|short.read_tps}); it is 67 tokens in ~40 ms, the same as drafting off read the time before, so noise at that size.

llama.cpp, unchanged, landed within {llama_drift.max} of the after-PR-169 run on every medium, large and xlarge number (median {llama_drift.median}). Its small-prompt first tokens moved up to +60% (59 → 37 ms on Gemma 4 E2B): times that small are not comparable run to run.
Nothing errored, and no row spilled.
